_schema: F4 per-op acceptance policy (DSv4-Flash authored kernels). DRAFT PROPOSAL for GPT Astra 6 review + USER ratification. Defines how a kernel output is machine-judged acceptable vs its AUTHORITATIVE oracle. Three layers: (0) tolerance-independent hard gates; (1) numerical acceptance vs the oracle; (2) discrete-decision/selection acceptance. NOT YET ENFORCED. The numerical TOLERANCES are a user design decision; the oracle selection, metric structure, and layer-0 gates are the executor's proposal and can be implemented before tolerances are set.
gate: F4 (machine-evaluated per-op acceptance policy + fail-closed bench/job exits)
design_principles: GATE ON THE DECISION THAT MATTERS: for the indexer the acceptance is the induced TOP-K SELECTION, not the raw logit values (reviewer evidence: fused-vs-tiled logits differ 0.045; a published-BF16 stage replay gives 0.092 max diff yet 511/512 selection — a raw-value bound would mis-judge; selection agreement is the real contract).

JUDGE AGAINST THE AUTHORITATIVE ORACLE: BF16/AMX approximation paths are compared to the published inference/kernel.py BF16 primitive (its rounding is authoritative), NOT the FP32 torch oracle; FP32 scalar paths are compared to the FP32 oracle.
COSINE ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT: pair cosine with max relative error on BOTH normal and heavy-tailed inputs (a loose cosine once hid a ~2.6e-3 error).
BIT-EXACT WHERE ACHIEVABLE: FP32 scalar paths are bit-deterministic across thread counts and should be required bit-exact (rel 0), not merely within tolerance.
FAIL CLOSED: every violation fails BOTH the benchmark and the job (nonzero exit); no print-and-continue.

layer0_hard_gates_tolerance_independent._note: Implementable immediately; needs NO user tolerance decision.
gates: output finiteness: no NaN/Inf in any output tensor
output shape + dtype == the declared op contract
input-domain guards hold (CPU device, dtype, rank, divisibility, scalar range) — the F9 TORCH_CHECK guards
thread-count determinism: identical output across {1, N} threads for the same code path
exit propagation: ANY violation -> nonzero bench exit AND nonzero SLURM job exit

layer1_numerical_vs_oracle._note: Tolerances PROPOSED; user ratifies. Evaluated on normal AND heavy-tailed inputs.

layer2_discrete_selection._note: The downstream decision. Tie rule PROPOSED; user ratifies.

proposed.tie_rule: indices whose score is within tie_eps of the k-th boundary score are EXEMPT from exact index match; compare the selected score MULTISET instead (prevents legitimate ties from failing)

indexer_logits.cpp.oracle: published inference/kernel.py BF16 indexer primitive (authoritative rounding); torch fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch as a secondary check
indexer_logits.cpp.layer1: cosine + relerr vs the BF16 primitive
indexer_logits.cpp.layer2: GATING criterion = the induced top-k selection agreement (with tie band); raw-logit diff alone is NOT the gate

indexer_topk.cpp.layer2: set-match 1.0 with the tie band; k==0 -> empty [N,0] int64

compressor.cpp.layer1: bit-exact (rel 0) preferred; else cosine+relerr at ALL 3 costed shapes (R=128/D=512, R=8/D=512, R=8/D=128), masked/overlap states included

sparse_attend.cpp.layer1: scalar tight (reviewer observed 4.3e-7); AMX looser vs the BF16 primitive (reviewer observed 2.5e-3) -> DECLARE the AMX bound; evaluate the full window+compressed 128/640/160 path, not only K=512 pre-gathered

sinkhorn.cpp.layer1: cosine on pre/post/comb + doubly-stochastic row/col-sum constraint within eps

user_decisions_required: the 6 tolerance knobs in layers.layer1_numerical_vs_oracle.proposed_bounds and layers.layer2_discrete_selection.proposed
confirm FP32 scalar paths must be bit-exact (executor recommends yes)
implementable_without_tolerances: bench + job nonzero-exit propagation on any failure
metric structure (cosine + relerr + selection, not cosine alone)
enforcement_plan: a per-op acceptance harness builds normal + heavy-tailed inputs, runs kernel + oracle, evaluates layers 0-2, and exits nonzero on ANY failure so the SLURM job fails. Layer-0 + exit propagation land immediately; layer-1/2 thresholds read the ratified values from this file once set.
